title: Morphisms of sheaves are determined by, and can be built from, their values on a basis
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal C$ a category, and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology, viewed as a full subcategory of the poset of opens. Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf on $X$ with values in $\mathcal C$. (a) For every family of morphisms $\psi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, compatible with the restrictions along inclusions $V\subseteq U$ of members of $\mathcal B$, there is exactly one morphism of presheaves $\Psi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ with $\Psi_U=\psi_U$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$; in particular two morphisms $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ which agree on every $U\in\mathcal B$ are equal. (b) If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf too and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism such that $\varphi_U$ is an isomorphism for every $U\in\mathcal B$, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Section 009H (sheaves on a basis): Lemma 009O (label lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence: restriction to a basis is an equivalence of sheaf categories, in particular fully faithful), with Lemmas 009R/009U for sheaves with algebraic structure and of modules
